articles.title: Resolving Go Application Performance Issues: CPU Usage and Memory Leaks with pprof and Flame Graphs
articles.excerpt: Introduction to Golang Profiling with pprof Profiling Go applications is not just a debugging exercise—it’s a survival skill in modern software development. As Go’s runtime schedules goroutines onto O…
articles.body: Introduction to Golang Profiling with pprof Profiling Go applications is not just a debugging exercise—it’s a survival skill in modern software development. As Go’s runtime schedules goroutines onto OS threads , the system’s efficiency hinges on how well these threads are utilized. pprof , Go’s built-in profiling tool, acts as a microscope, capturing runtime data via sampling to expose CPU, memory, block, and mutex behaviors. Without it, performance issues like high CPU usage or memory leaks remain invisible, silently degrading application reliability and scalability. Consider CPU usage: inefficient algorithms or busy-waiting loops force the CPU to execute redundant instructions , consuming cycles that could be allocated to other tasks.

articles.body: Football prediction sites rarely show their misses. Records get edited, bad months vanish, and "verified" win rates can't be checked by anyone. We went the other way. Every prediction we publish is written to the database before kick-off, settled automatically at full time, and never edited or deleted afterwards. The whole ledger is a plain CSV that anyone can download. What's in it 25,816 settled predictions across 2,519 matches in 60+ competitions: Premier League, La Liga, Serie A, Bundesliga, MLS, Liga MX, the Champions League and many more. It starts on 16 Aug 2026 and grows every matchday. Rows are only ever appended.

articles.body: Most multi-entry products grow separate implementations behind the same name. An open-source agent framework for HarmonyOS development (hmharness, MIT) just lived through this pit — and the user who spotted it asked one question: "It is the same AI, why is it so different?" The scene: the same Dependabot task, run from two entry points. The BrowserOS assistant panel (ACP protocol) crushed it — read mails, GHSA forensics, npm fix, tests 7/7, draft PR, all in one flow. The extension sidebar stumbled constantly. The root cause had a name: same-name, different-engine. The panel ran the full runAgentTask (complete tool registry, real system prompts with memory/skills/insights, session continuity, approval cards). The sidebar was an early hand-rolled minimal chat loop.

articles.title: Two AI chats, one game board, and a server that trusts neither
articles.excerpt: Every game in Fyreflock was written for two browsers in lockstep, with no referee anywhere. That held up right until I let a language model take a seat, because a model reads everything it's handed, a…
articles.body: Every game in Fyreflock was written for two browsers in lockstep, with no referee anywhere. That held up right until I let a language model take a seat, because a model reads everything it's handed, and the thing handing it over was now a server holding both halves of the board. Some context. Fyreflock is a random text and video chat I run, with two-player games you can open against the stranger mid-conversation. It also has an MCP connector for Claude, ChatGPT and Claude Code ( github.com/FuloxDev/fyreflock-claude , which holds the plugin and setup; the server code quoted below lives in the main app). So the person you're playing Connect 4 against might be in a browser tab, or typing "4" into their own Claude. This is how the games survived that.

articles.body: ESA/Webb, NASA & CSA, E. Sabbi, M. Zamani (ESA/Webb); Acknowledgement: M. H. Özsaraç In this Webb image released on Oct. 22, 2026, we see a turbulent cauldron of star formation filled with dense clumps of gas. This region is named N159 and is located 161,000 light-years away in the Large Magellanic Cloud, one of the satellite galaxies orbiting the Milky Way galaxy. This region has a lower metallicity (proportion of elements that are heavier than helium and hydrogen) than the Milky Way, giving astronomers an opportunity to learn more about conditions found in the early universe and how stars formed under those conditions. articles.title: Satellites watch an escaping Antarctic iceberg | Space photo of the day for Oct. 28, 2026
articles.excerpt: Iceberg A-81 escaping the Weddell Sea and drifting near the edge of South Georgia's underwater shelf.
articles.body: Iceberg A-81 escaping the Weddell Sea and drifting near the edge of South Georgia's underwater shelf. The image was captured on Oct. 20, 2026. (Image credit: NASA Earth Observatory/Michala Garrison) An iceberg has quickly escaped from the Weddell Sea in Antarctica, on its way to an icy new destination. What is it? As captured by a satellite in orbit, the Antarctic iceberg A-81 has quite quickly (for an iceberg) parted ways from its icy home, breaking off to drift toward a shallow underwater shelf in Georgia. The 600-square-mile (1,550-square-kilometer) iceberg first broke off from the Brunt Ice Shelf in January of 2023. Now, generally speaking, giant icebergs don't travel that fast.
